title: pvYoungsMaterialInterface
body:
## pvYoungsMaterialInterface

Reconstructs sharp material interfaces in mixed cells of Eulerian or ALE multi-material simulations (e.g. CTH or other volume-of-fluid output) with Youngs' method: in each cell the material is bounded by a plane perpendicular to its interface normal, placed so the cut volume matches the cell's volume fraction. Input is a composite dataset with one cell-centred volume fraction array per material and, ideally, a 3-component cell normal array per material. Output is a multiblock with one block per material (in VolumeFractionArrays order) holding the interface polygons or, with FillMaterial (ParaView default), the material's volume.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Without a normal array for a material, VTK uses the +x direction, so interfaces come out as planes perpendicular to x; supply normals (e.g. from the volume-fraction gradient).
- AxisSymetric is true by ParaView default and treats 2-D meshes as axisymmetric (volumes of revolution); set it false for planar 2-D data.
- Only 2-D and 3-D cells are processed and input must be composite (e.g. multiblock); wrap a single mesh with pvGroupDatasets first.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `YoungsMaterialInterface`. Identity: `filters/YoungsMaterialInterface`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. Accepted data: composite data (multiblock or partitioned collections) (vtkCompositeDataSet). The input needs at least one cell-centred array with 1 component. | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkCompositeDataSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AxisSymetric` | For 2-D cells, treats the mesh as an axisymmetric section (volume of revolution about the axis) when placing interfaces, so cut positions honour revolved volumes rather than planar areas. It has no effect on 3-D cells. Native name keeps ParaView's spelling. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `FillMaterial` | When true, each material block contains the material's volume: pure cells whole plus the material side of every cut mixed cell. When false, only the interface itself is output (polygons in 3-D, lines in 2-D) and pure cells are omitted. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `InverseNormal` | Flips the sign of every material normal before the interface is placed, which moves the material to the other side of its interface plane. Use it when the supplied normals point out of the material (e.g. a plain volume-fraction gradient points into it). | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `NormalArrays` | Assigns an interface-normal cell array to materials, as a flat list of pairs [volume-fraction array, normal array, volume-fraction array, normal array, …]. Each normal array is a 3-component cell array giving the interface orientation for that material; materials without one get a degenerate normal replaced by +x. Complete tuples of 2 values. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `OnionPeel` | When true, materials are processed in order within each cell and all use the first material's normal, like layers of an onion, which keeps nested interfaces parallel and avoids overlaps in cells with three or more materials. When false, each material uses its own normal. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `OrderingArrays` | Assigns an ordering cell array to materials, as a flat list of pairs [volume-fraction array, ordering array, …]. In each cell, materials are processed in ascending order of their ordering value (descending with ReverseMaterialOrder), which matters with OnionPeel. Materials without one have ordering 0 and keep their VolumeFractionArrays order. Complete tuples of 2 values. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `ReverseMaterialOrder` | Reverses the order in which materials are processed in each cell (descending ordering value instead of ascending, or reverse list order without ordering arrays). With OnionPeel this changes which material forms the inner layer. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `UseFractionAsDistance` | When true, the volume-fraction value is used directly as the distance of the interface plane from the cell origin along the normal, instead of solving for the plane that matches the volume fraction; the fraction range thresholds are then bypassed. Use it only when the arrays store plane distances (e.g. level-set style data). | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `VolumeFractionArrays` | Names of the cell-centred volume-fraction arrays (values 0 to 1), one per material; the list order is the material index and the order of the output blocks. Blocks lacking an array simply contribute nothing for that material. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `VolumeFractionRange` | Thresholds [min, max] on a material's volume fraction in a cell: at or below min the cell is treated as empty of that material, at or above max as full (copied whole only when FillMaterial is true), and in between an interface is reconstructed. Narrowing the range removes slivers from nearly pure cells. | `{"items":{"maximum":1.0,"minimum":0.0,"type":"number"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[0.0,0.0]` |
